title: Suspected Meniscal Injury MRI
source_citation: International guideline; not Philippine CPG (AAOS Acute Isolated Meniscal Pathology)
excerpt_text: For suspected acute isolated meniscal pathology, MRI can help confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment when the clinical assessment supports internal derangement; this is an international fallback, not Philippine policy.

title: DOH Chest X-Ray Guidance for Suspected CAP
source_citation: Philippine DOH Guidelines for Community-Acquired Pneumonia (Primary Healthcare Manual)
excerpt_text: When the clinical picture supports community-acquired pneumonia, chest X-ray helps confirm pneumonia, assess severity, and distinguish it from other disease; it is not required for every cough.

title: Philippine Knee Osteoarthritis Management
excerpt_text: Management of knee osteoarthritis should start with individualized non-drug care such as exercise, weight management, and physical modalities; medicines are selected with attention to benefits, harms, and patient factors.

title: Philippine Hypertension Management
excerpt_text: Adult hypertension is generally defined using repeated office blood-pressure measurements at or above 140/90 mmHg; confirm the diagnosis when appropriate and individualize treatment targets.

title: Philippine Diabetes Diagnosis and Management
excerpt_text: Diabetes care combines diagnostic confirmation, cardiovascular-risk assessment, lifestyle support, individualized glucose targets, and regular monitoring for complications.

title: Philippine Prediabetes Prevention
excerpt_text: People with prediabetes should receive structured lifestyle support focused on healthy eating, physical activity, weight management, and periodic reassessment for progression to diabetes.

title: Philippine Dyslipidemia Management
excerpt_text: Lifestyle measures are recommended for Filipino patients with dyslipidemia; lipid-lowering treatment is based on overall cardiovascular risk, diabetes status, and lipid results.

title: Philippine Adult Obesity Care
excerpt_text: Assessment of obesity should include health risks and patient goals; counseling on nutrition, physical activity, and sustainable weight reduction is part of primary care.

title: Chronic Kidney Disease Follow-up
excerpt_text: Chronic kidney disease follow-up should monitor kidney function, urine findings, blood pressure, medication risks, and cardiovascular risk, with referral when severity or complications require specialist care.

title: Hypothyroidism Follow-up
excerpt_text: Evaluate symptoms and thyroid testing together, then adjust treatment and follow-up intervals to the patient’s response, pregnancy status, age, and comorbidities.

title: Philippine Coronary Disease Risk Management
excerpt_text: Patients with established coronary disease need risk-factor treatment, medication review, symptom assessment, and escalation or referral when symptoms suggest instability.

title: Heart Failure Follow-up
excerpt_text: Heart-failure follow-up should assess congestion, symptoms, adherence, renal function, and treatment tolerance, with urgent escalation for worsening breathlessness or instability.

title: Atrial Fibrillation Assessment
excerpt_text: Evaluate suspected atrial fibrillation with a 12-lead ECG and assess stroke and bleeding risks before selecting a management plan; this is an international fallback, not Philippine policy.

title: Chest Pain ECG Assessment
excerpt_text: Acute or unexplained chest pain requires clinical risk assessment and a timely ECG when a cardiac cause is possible; this international fallback is not Philippine policy.

title: Philippine Community Acquired Pneumonia
excerpt_text: Evaluate suspected community-acquired pneumonia using symptoms, examination, oxygenation, and chest imaging when indicated, then determine outpatient versus higher-level care from severity and risk.

title: Philippine Asthma Diagnosis and Management
excerpt_text: Asthma diagnosis should be supported by variable respiratory symptoms and objective lung-function assessment when feasible; treatment and follow-up are adjusted to control and exacerbation risk.

title: Philippine COPD Diagnosis and Management
excerpt_text: COPD assessment includes symptoms, exposure history, and spirometry; management combines smoking cessation, vaccination, inhaled treatment, rehabilitation, and exacerbation planning.

title: Acute Upper Respiratory Infection Care
excerpt_text: Most uncomplicated upper-respiratory infections are managed with supportive care and safety-net advice; assess for red flags, complications, or an alternate diagnosis before prescribing antibiotics.

title: Acute Bronchitis Chest Imaging
excerpt_text: Routine chest imaging is not indicated for uncomplicated acute bronchitis; consider imaging or referral when pneumonia, severe illness, or another serious cause is suspected.

title: Philippine Tuberculosis Screening
excerpt_text: Adults and children with tuberculosis symptoms or risk factors should receive symptom screening and appropriate testing, including chest imaging or molecular testing according to the national TB pathway.

title: Philippine Dengue Primary Care
excerpt_text: For suspected dengue, assess warning signs, hydration, bleeding risk, and disease phase; provide close follow-up or referral when warning signs or severe disease are present.

title: Philippine Acute Infectious Diarrhea
excerpt_text: Assess dehydration and severity first; oral rehydration is central for suitable patients, while testing, antibiotics, or referral depend on clinical features and risk.

title: Philippine Urinary Tract Infection
excerpt_text: Diagnose urinary-tract infection from symptoms and appropriate urine testing when indicated, distinguishing uncomplicated cystitis from pyelonephritis, recurrence, pregnancy, and complicated infection.

title: Philippine Hepatitis B Care
excerpt_text: Chronic hepatitis B care includes confirmation, staging, liver-risk assessment, monitoring, prevention of transmission, and referral for treatment decisions when indicated.

title: GERD Symptom Management
excerpt_text: Typical reflux symptoms can be managed with lifestyle advice and an appropriate empiric approach, while alarm features or refractory symptoms require further evaluation; this is an international fallback.

title: Right Upper Quadrant Pain Ultrasound
excerpt_text: Ultrasound is an appropriate first imaging test for suspected biliary or right-upper-quadrant pathology; clinical examination and urgent referral remain necessary for severe or unstable presentations.

title: Philippine Gout Management
excerpt_text: Gout care combines confirmation when feasible, acute-attack treatment, urate-lowering decisions, lifestyle counseling, and monitoring for renal and cardiovascular comorbidity.

title: Philippine Osteoporosis and Fragility Fracture Prevention
excerpt_text: Assess fracture risk and modifiable factors; bone-density testing and pharmacologic prevention are considered according to risk, age, fracture history, and clinical context.

title: Low Back Pain Primary Care
excerpt_text: Most uncomplicated low-back pain is initially managed with education, activity, and conservative care; urgent imaging or referral is reserved for red flags or concerning neurologic findings.

title: Anemia Evaluation
excerpt_text: Evaluate anemia with history, examination, and targeted laboratory testing to identify blood loss, nutritional deficiency, chronic disease, or other causes before treatment.

title: Migraine Primary Care
excerpt_text: Diagnose migraine clinically when the pattern is typical, address triggers and acute treatment, and investigate or refer urgently when headache features are atypical or dangerous.

title: Dermatitis Primary Care
excerpt_text: Assess dermatitis from morphology, distribution, exposures, and infection clues; use skin care and appropriate topical treatment while referring atypical, severe, or treatment-resistant disease.

title: Philippine Depression in Primary Care
source_citation: PAFP Adult Depression in Primary Care
excerpt_text: Screening should be paired with assessment of severity, safety, function, comorbidity, and patient preference; urgent safety concerns require immediate escalation.

title: Anxiety in Primary Care
excerpt_text: Assess anxiety symptoms, impairment, substance use, medical contributors, and safety; offer evidence-based psychosocial care and referral when severity or risk exceeds primary-care support.

title: Philippine Periodic Health Examination
excerpt_text: A periodic health examination should be individualized to age, sex, risks, immunization status, lifestyle, and evidence-based screening rather than applying every test to every patient.

title: Philippine Immunization Counseling
excerpt_text: Offer vaccination according to age, risk, prior doses, pregnancy status, occupation, and current Philippine recommendations, documenting counseling and contraindication review.

title: Preventive Breast Screening
excerpt_text: Breast-cancer screening should use shared decision-making and the locally applicable age and risk recommendations; do not treat a screening code as proof that imaging is clinically required.

title: Preventive Colorectal Screening
excerpt_text: Offer colorectal-cancer screening according to age, family history, symptoms, and available test options; symptomatic patients require diagnostic evaluation rather than routine screening alone.

title: Philippine Prenatal Care
excerpt_text: Prenatal care includes gestational-age assessment, maternal and fetal risk review, routine laboratory and preventive care, counseling, and timely referral for danger signs or high-risk pregnancy.

title: Diabetes in Pregnancy
excerpt_text: Pregnancy with diabetes requires coordinated glucose monitoring, nutrition and medication review, maternal-fetal risk assessment, and obstetric follow-up tailored to gestational age and complications.

title: Pediatric Dengue Primary Care
excerpt_text: In children with suspected dengue, assess warning signs, hydration, bleeding, and disease phase repeatedly because clinical status can change quickly; refer when severe features appear.

title: Pediatric Preventive Health Examination
excerpt_text: Pediatric preventive visits should cover growth, development, nutrition, immunization, safety, and age-appropriate screening, with referral for abnormal findings or developmental concerns.
